text:
Mikaela: Heads-up — kicked off a targeted recompute for the EU agg window and we're seeing routing pressure + quota spikes. Console shows Dedicated pool saturating, some tenant requests getting 429s. Anyone online? :eyes:
Samir: on it. which job id? I can throttle at submitter side or add a token-bucket in the backfill coordinator.
Mikaela: job=2023-eu-recompute-741, launched from the console bulk-recompute flow. InfraBot logged the job at 3032104550.
InfraBot: Job 2023-eu-recompute-741 queued -> running on pool-dedicated-eu-1. Estimated tokens ~ 4.2M.
Rajat: Oof, that's big. Agree we should avoid everyone hitting the same routing policy. Suggest per-tenant leaky-bucket and a global backfill lane with low priority.
Tara: UX note — the console bulk-recompute button currently shows a single progress bar. Need to surface "priority lane" and "estimated cost" BEFORE submit to avoid surprise runs. filed UX ticket: #3589.
Samir: quick mitigation: set job concurrency=8 and rate_limit=20 tokens/sec for now. Patch config and drain excess workers.
Jo: Can we also enable KV-cache rehydrate first for hot tenants to reduce recompute work? It shaves off a lot for prefix-heavy traffic.
Mikaela: good call — Jo, can you add a preflight step to the coordinator that checks KV cache hit rate and skips recompute for >90% hit tenants?
Jo: yep. I can add that as a flag: `--skip-if-kv-hit-rate>=0.9`. Will test locally.
Samir: config snippet I'm going to deploy to the coordinator (quick):
```yaml
backfill: 
  concurrency: 8
  rate_limit_tokens_per_sec: 20
  priority: low
  per_tenant_bucket: true
  bucket_capacity: 200
```
Rajat: long-term we should expose per-tenant ETA + cost estimate on the console and a "run in canary lane" toggle (run on 1% of tenants first). Otherwise ops gets paged.
Tara: agreed. UX suggestion: on the bulk flow, show a compact "cost slider" that defaults to conservative throttles. Owners can bump it.
Mikaela: infra alert: some control-plane API 503s observed; looks like coordinator's submitter endpoint got overloaded during burst. We might need to add a submit queue and backpressure responses.
Samir: I'll add a client-side backoff and 429->retry jitter. Also will flip the coordinator to accept queue-only when overload detected.
Jo: small script to stagger existing running backfills by tenant hash (mod 60) to distribute load over a minute. Posting script: `python tools/stagger_backfills.py --job 2023-eu-recompute-741 --mod 60`
Mikaela: nice. After Samir's patch + Jo's preflight+stagger we'll re-evaluate. Can someone add a chart to the console dashboard showing "backfill lanes vs normal traffic" and the routing policy used per request? That would help triage.
Rajat: I'll add the metrics in the telemetry plan: `backfill_lane{tenant, lane}` and `routing_policy_decision{route, reason}`. Then Tara can wire the dashboard.
Tara: will wire a small card under "Jobs" with lane breakdown + estimated cost. UX note: make it collapsible to avoid noise.
Samir: deployed rate-limit patch to coordinator v0.41.3 (PR https://github.com/redwood/recompute/pull/642). Rolling canary to 10% of hosts first.
InfraBot: Deployment v0.41.3 -> canary hosts (10%) at 3032104740; all checks passing.
Mikaela: monitoring looks better — 429s down, dedicated pool CPU trending down. Leave this thread for runbook updates and UX ticket linking.
Rajat: follow-up items: (1) per-tenant ETA on console, (2) submit queue + backpressure on control-plane, (3) expose lane metrics in telemetry. I'll own 1 & 3.
Tara: I'll own 2 (filed as infra-ux #3590 and linked to #3589).
Jo: I'll PR the preflight kv check and stagger tool by EOD.
Samir: I'll bake in per-tenant bucket enforcement and add docs for default throttles.
Mikaela: thanks — keeping this open until all items are in. :thumbsup:
